content: I tried solving this puzzle with two different solutions I could think of. The first being the most obvious witch is by actually implementing and counting recursive calls, and the second was to count using breadth first search since the calls form a binary tree. Both solutions timed out after "Slower". I spent some time trying to figure out the math but I couldn't get it so I had to give up or else my head was gonna explode :P . Anyway, that was my experience and I'll need to study your solution later because I still don't get it.

Goal
* 1st paragraph: Please add "(other than the initial two)" after "each number".

* Consider rewording the middle paragraph to avoid mixing one level of recursion with another:

Whenever n > 1, a call to fib(n) recursively calls fib(n-1) and fib(n-2). Those calls recursively call fib() in the same way until reaching fib(0) or fib(1), which return immediately.

Cases
* Trivial 2 (Validator 7): Please change n to 0.

* Please move the Trivial 1 and Trivial 2 case pairs so that they appear consecutively.

* Impossible (Validator 11) is the only case whose output isn't a 32-bit integer. Please modify the test so that it features the same scenario.

Thanks.
Interesting, I had engineered the test cases such that implementing the pseudocode directly would only fail at "Improbable" (validator) / "Impossible" (test). Which language did you use?
Lua and JS. But you're right. These tests and validators after "Slower" takes too long for unoptimized solutions. In my experience, fib recursion passed on "Improbable" but the BFS didn't
The output when n = 45 is still a 32-bit integer. Please revise the case. Thanks.
